evidence: Table 8-1, row 'H100 peak FP16 TFLOPS': 'metric: H100 peak FP16 TFLOPS | value: ~989 TFLOPS [1P: NVIDIA H100 datasheet]'. The Preface (p.xiv) states: "Throughout this book the SI convention applies: K = 1,000 and M = 1,000,000 for token counts." The SI convention for unit prefixes requires the numeric value and unit symbol to be written as a single token without an intervening space only for values <1000 in some style guides; however, the book inconsistently writes '~989 TFLOPS' (space present, consistent) vs elsewhere '989 TFLOPS' vs '~0.989 PFLOPS' — the mixed prefix units (TFLOPS, PFLOPS, GFLOP, GFLOP/token) within the same table and same sentence (e.g. p.161 '346.15 TFLOPS ÷ 140 GFLOP/token = 2,472.5') mix FLOP (operation count) and FLOPS (rate) without ever defining the FLOPS notation in the book's own Terminology section (Preface p.xiv defines TTFT, HBM, VRAM, but not FLOP vs FLOPS).
issue: The notation FLOP vs FLOPS is never explicitly defined in the book's Terminology or Reading Conventions sections (Preface p.xiv), yet Table 8-1 and the surrounding prose mix them freely ('346.15 TFLOPS ÷ 140 GFLOP/token'). A reader unfamiliar with the convention could read 'GFLOP/token' as a rate. The Preface defines every other abbreviation it uses (TTFT, HBM, VRAM, MFU) but omits FLOPS.
fix_instruction: Add FLOP and FLOPS to the Terminology paragraph in the Preface (p.xiv): 'FLOP = one floating-point operation (count); FLOPS = floating-point operations per second (rate). Throughout, FLOP without S is a count and FLOPS with S is a rate.' This is a one-sentence fix that prevents misreading in every roofline calculation.

evidence: p.62, Canonical Workload box, 'Total input' row: '9,200 tokens' and 'Output' row: '300 tokens'. Below the box: 'The two derived rates most chapters cite: at 10 rps the input demand is ~92,000 tokens/s (9,200 × 10) and output ~3,000 tokens/s (300 × 10)'. But the Canonical Workload box (p.62-63) lists the same values as '1,200 tokens', '8,000 tokens', '9,200 tokens', '300 tokens' — with NO tilde on the individual components (1,200 not ~1,200) while the box's own 'Mean request service time' row carries '~10 s' with a tilde. The tilde is applied inconsistently within the same box: some rows have '~' (10 rps, ~100 active users, ~86 requests) and some do not (1,200 tokens, 8,000 tokens, 9,200 tokens, 300 tokens).
issue: The Canonical Workload box (p.62-64) inconsistently applies the approximation marker '~' to its values: traffic rows say '~10 rps' and '~100 active users' but token-count rows say '1,200 tokens' and '9,200 tokens' without '~', while Table 4-1 (p.58) writes '~1,200 prompt + ~8,000 retrieved context ≈ 9,200 tokens'. The same values appear with and without the approximation marker across two tables in the same chapter, making it unclear which are exact inputs and which are rounded.
fix_instruction: Standardize: either apply '~' to every canonical-scenario input in the Canonical Workload box (matching Table 4-1's style) or remove it from Table 4-1 and state once in the box header that all values are approximate. evidence: p.144: 'The contrast between these two floors — inference ~164.1 GB for a 70B model at FP16 with 9.2K input (140 + 24.1; the 9.5K-max is 164.9 ≈ 165 GB) [canonical scenario][DERIVED], fine-tuning exceeding 1 TB [canonical scenario][DERIVED]'. Then p.149: 'the ~500 GB headroom (Ch. 4/7, single-request) and the ~436 GB KV budget (Ch. 17, concurrency) answer different questions'. The ~500 GB is 640 − 140 = 500 (weights subtracted from pool, KV not yet subtracted). The ~436 GB is 640 − 140 − 64 = 436 (weights and runtime reserve subtracted). Both are labeled 'headroom' or 'budget' in the same paragraph without the ~64 GB runtime reserve being mentioned as the differentiating term. The sentence 'the ~500 GB headroom ... and the ~436 GB KV budget ... answer different questions' does not state that the 64 GB difference IS the runtime reserve — a reader must cross-reference §7.1 (p.144) to understand why the two numbers differ by 64 GB.
issue: Two different 'headroom/budget' figures (~500 GB and ~436 GB) are cited side by side on p.149 without stating that the 64 GB difference is the runtime/workspace reserve. The text says they 'answer different questions' but does not name the arithmetic that separates them (500 = 640−140; 436 = 640−140−64). A reader encountering only p.149 cannot reconcile the two numbers without jumping to §7.1.
fix_instruction: On p.149, after 'answer different questions', add the one-clause reconciliation: '(~500 GB = 640 − 140 weights, before the ~64 GB runtime reserve; ~436 GB = 640 − 140 − 64, after it)'. This makes the two figures self-explanatory at the point of use.

evidence: p.119, §6.8: 'prefix caching is a partial mitigation (~13% of prefill FLOPs), not the fix for the 40 rps prefill queue'. The ~13% figure comes from p.117 (§6.3.4): 'the byte-identical share is at most the fixed system/instruction portion of the ~1,200-token prompt ... so ~13% of prefill FLOPs (the whole-slot case) is an upper bound on the cacheable fraction'. 1,200 ÷ 9,200 = 13.04%. The text calls it '~13%' on both pages. However, p.117 also says 'the 8K retrieved block differs per query and the 1,200-token slot carries the query itself (Ch 4 Table 4-1)', meaning the cacheable fraction could be LESS than 13% (the query part of the 1,200 tokens is not cacheable across queries). The '~13% (the whole-slot case)' phrasing acknowledges this but p.119 drops the '(the whole-slot case)' qualifier and the 'upper bound' language, presenting '~13% of prefill FLOPs' as a flat figure rather than an upper bound.
issue: The '~13% of prefill FLOPs' figure loses its 'upper bound' and '(the whole-slot case)' qualifiers when restated on p.119 (§6.8). On p.117 it is explicitly an upper bound ('at most', 'upper bound on the cacheable fraction'); on p.119 it appears as a bare quantity ('~13% of prefill FLOPs'), which a reader could take as a measured or expected value rather than a ceiling.
fix_instruction: On p.119, restore the qualifier: change '~13% of prefill FLOPs' to '~13% of prefill FLOPs (an upper bound; the cacheable fraction is smaller once the query tokens are excluded)' or simply '~≤13% of prefill FLOPs (upper bound, §6.3.4)'.

evidence: p.145, §7.7, third bullet: '(a) decode-time KV offload to CPU DRAM trades TPOT/ITL and KV capacity, not TTFT (TTFT is already complete when decode starts); (b) prefix/KV reuse loaded from CPU can reduce TTFT for cache-hit requests — the vLLM KV Offloading Connector's 2–22× figure is defined in Ch 6 (TTFT metric, warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark) [S7][1P][FACT] and is highly prompt-size-dependent.' The label [S7][1P][FACT] is attached to a compound sentence that includes both (i) a definitional cross-reference (which TTFT metric is used) and (ii) a factual claim (the 2–22× figure exists and is warm-cache-specific). issue: The [S7][1P][FACT] label on p.145 covers a sentence that mixes a cross-reference, a factual figure, and an unlabeled interpretive qualifier ('highly prompt-size-dependent'). The interpretive qualifier appears only on p.145 and has no provenance label — it is the book's own interpretation of the source, not a first-party fact. Meanwhile the p.118 version of the same claim omits this qualifier entirely, creating two slightly different restatements of the same source claim.
fix_instruction: Split the sentence: (1) keep [S7][1P][FACT] on 'the vLLM KV Offloading Connector's 2–22× figure ... warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark'; (2) tag 'highly prompt-size-dependent' as [DERIVED] or [HYPOTHESIS] (it is the book's inference from the benchmark description); (3) either add the same qualifier to p.118 or remove it from p.145 for consistency.

evidence: p.62, Canonical Workload box: 'Execution occupancy: ~86 requests at 10 rps (Wexec ≈ 8.6 s); ~344 at 40 rps — [canonical scenario][DERIVED] via Little's Law L = λ × Wexec'. The parenthetical says 'Wexec ≈ 8.6 s'. The derivation in the same box (p.62-63, 'Mean request service time' row) states: 'The modelled components are retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s = ~8.7 s'. And: 'The occupancy service time is the derived Wexec = prefill + decode ≈ 8.58 s (shown as 8.6 s)'. So 8.58 s is rounded to 8.6 s. Checking: 10 × 8.58 = 85.8 ≈ 86 ✓; 40 × 8.58 = 343.2 ≈ 344 ✓; 10 × 8.6 = 86 ✓; 40 × 8.6 = 344 ✓. The arithmetic is correct. However, the box shows 'Wexec ≈ 8.6 s' in the occupancy row while the service-time row shows '= ~8.7 s' for the retrieval+prefill+decode total — two different rounded service times (8.6 and 8.7) appear in the same box for what is conceptually related quantities, distinguished only by whether retrieval is included. The box does explain this in the service-time row ('The occupancy service time is the derived Wexec = prefill + decode ≈ 8.58 s ... it excludes the ~120 ms retrieval term') but the two numbers (8.6 and 8.7) are never placed side by side with an explicit 'these differ by the retrieval term' note in the occupancy row itself.
issue: Two service times (8.6 s for occupancy, 8.7 s for planning) appear in the same Canonical Workload box without the occupancy row itself stating why it differs from the planning figure. The explanation exists in the service-time row's footnote but a reader scanning the occupancy row alone sees 'Wexec ≈ 8.6 s' and a nearby '= ~8.7 s' with no inline reconciliation. This is a minor clarity issue: the distinction IS documented, just not at the point where the second number appears.
fix_instruction: In the Execution occupancy row, append to 'Wexec ≈ 8.6 s' the parenthetical '(excludes retrieval; the ~10 s planning headline includes it — see service-time row)'. This makes the two service times self-reconciling at each point of use.

evidence: p.29, §2.3: 'An NVIDIA H100 delivers ~989 TFLOPS (BF16 dense tensor-core peak, without sparsity) [1P][FACT], which is 0.989 PFLOPS. (Here and throughout we quote the dense, no-sparsity tensor-core peak for any precision; NVIDIA's datasheet prints the 2× with-sparsity figure — 1,979 TFLOPS for FP16/BF16 — as its headline number, so a dense-vs-sparse note is required even in vendor material.)' The text says 'NVIDIA's datasheet prints the 2× with-sparsity figure — 1,979 TFLOPS for FP16/BF16 — as its headline number'. Checking: 989 × 2 = 1,978, not 1,979. The actual NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet figure is 1,979 TFLOPS (with sparsity). The book correctly states 1,979, and 989 × 2 = 1,978 ≈ 1,979 (the datasheet rounds up). However, the text writes '1,979 TFLOPS' and elsewhere (p.161, Table 8-1) writes '~1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2' — the division 1,979 ÷ 2 = 989.5, which the book presents as '989 TFLOPS'. The half-TFLOP rounding (989.5 → 989) is never acknowledged. This is a rounding of a vendor-published figure, presented as if exact.
issue: Table 8-1 (p.161) derives the dense peak as '1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2' = 989 TFLOPS, but 1,979 ÷ 2 = 989.5. The half-TFLOP is silently truncated to 989. The vendor's dense figure may itself be 989 or 989.5 — the book presents the division as producing exactly 989 without noting the rounding. This is a very minor rounding presentation issue, not an arithmetic error (989.5 ≈ 989), but the derivation '1,979 ÷ 2' implies an exact halving that yields a non-integer.
fix_instruction: In Table 8-1's derivation cell, write '1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2 ≈ 989 TFLOPS (vendor dense figure, rounded)' or simply cite the dense figure directly from the datasheet rather than deriving it by halving the sparse figure.
